subject: Re: Redwood vs hyperscalers — TCO follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Taylor Reed <taylor@finpay.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay call recap — latency/cost goals + next steps

Thanks for the call today, Aditya — useful conversation. Quick recap and our priorities so we can align tests: 

Summary:
- We're evaluating for a customer-facing assistant (multi-turn, average response 120 tokens) and nightly batch embeddings for search.
- Key metrics: p50 latency < 250ms for short responses, p95 < 800ms, per-1M-token TCO target <$5 (all-in).
- We will compare Redwood against AWS Bedrock (Inference), Anthropic/Claude API, and OpenAI for both hosted ease and TCO.

Immediate asks (from FinPay):
1) Raw per-1M token cost for text gen at our expected prompt/response ratio (1:3).
2) Guidance on batching and cache hit assumptions — what's realistic for a PB-scale customer?
3) A proposed 2-week bench plan we can run in parallel to your environment + our subset.

Next steps we agreed on:
- Redwood to provide a short TCO sheet (per-1M token comparatives + assumptions).
- Run a micro-benchmark (1M tokens) with and without batching; measure p50/p95 and throughput.
- We (FinPay) will share sample prompts and a 48-hour window to run tests.

Thanks,
Taylor Reed
Head of AI Platform, FinPay

Attachment: sample-prompts.csv (we uploaded to your drive)
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay call recap — latency/cost goals + next steps

Appreciate the clear summary, Taylor — copied Marcus and Marissa to coordinate the bench. Below is the TCO snapshot and the assumptions used. We'll attach a spreadsheet with line-item math.

High-level per-1M-token TCO (text generation, 1:3 prompt:response, avg response 120 tokens):
- Redwood (hosted/routed to dedicated pool, default batching + KV caching): ~$2.60 per 1M tokens
- OpenAI (gpt-4o-style): ~$3.95 per 1M tokens
- Anthropic (Claude-infer): ~$4.40 per 1M tokens
- AWS Bedrock (inference endpoints): ~$5.10 per 1M tokens

Key assumptions (spreadsheet has line-by-line):
- Tokenization: 1 token ≈ 0.75 words, average prompt length 40 tokens, response 120 tokens
- Throughput optimizations: batching (batch size 8–16) and prefix/KV cache with 40% hit rate for repetitive prompts
- Dedicated pool pricing amortized into per-token (includes reserved capacity discounts)
- Networking and small infra margin factored in (10%)

What moves the needle:
- Batching: increases throughput and reduces per-token GPU time. At batch sizes 8–16 we see ~25–40% per-token reduction depending on model and sequence length.
- Cache hit rate: each cache hit can reduce end-to-end compute by 20–60% depending on prompt prefix length.
- Model size / quantization: using 8-bit quantized variants gives 15–30% cost reduction with minor latency impact on most workloads.

Attached: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-tco.xlsx (high-level assumptions and sensitivity). Marcus: can you add the bench plan and the specific API payloads?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-tco.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor@finpay.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay call recap — bench plan & sample requests

Thanks, team — below is a concrete, minimal bench plan we can run (2 parts). Marcus here (head of solutions engineering) — I'll run the Redwood side and help with scripts.

Bench Plan (2-week; first window we agreed is Mon Jul 13):
1) Micro-bench (3 days):
  - 1M tokens gen test for 3 settings: no batching, batching (B=8), batching (B=16). Measure p50/p95, throughput (tokens/sec), and GPU utilization.
  - Repeat with KV cache enabled (we'll preload common prefixes) and capture cache hit rate.
  - Run same payloads against your sample prompts and our API (we'll run an apples-to-apples client).
2) Production-sim test (4 days):
  - Simulate realistic traffic (multi-turn with 1:3 ratio) at target concurrency to measure end-to-end latencies and error rates.

Data we'll capture per run (CSV):
- timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, batch_size, cache_hit (true/false), gpu_util_pct

Control variables / notes:
- To make cost comparable we will: use same model family where possible, apply equal quantization settings, and include network egress where applicable.
- We'll provide a small harness (k6 + python) and a Redwood-config file to ensure consistent batching and KV settings.

Preliminary cost sensitivity (from our side):
- If cache hit >= 40% and batching B=8, per-1M token cost drops ~30% from the baseline. Example: Redwood baseline $2.60 → $1.82.
- Hyperscalers with managed endpoints often have higher per-token compute plus higher network/overhead; they benefit from batching but less from prefix caching unless you run close to the model (private/dedicated).

Attachments: benchmark-plan.md (scripts and k6 scenarios), mau-benchmark-results.pdf (example from a similar customer).

Ask: Taylor — can you confirm a 48-hour window next week when FinPay can point their traffic and share sample prompt set? We'll coordinate exact times.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
